newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Wing Tai plans regional expansion.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Wing Tai plans regional expansion.

text.p: Property developer Wing Tai Holdings plans to regionalise and focus on Hong Kong, Malaysia and China in addition to Singapore, company officials told a briefing on results announced on Monday.

"We will now devote time and efforts in growing the business and developing a long term presence in each of these markets. Singapore, Malaysia, Hong Kong and eventually, China will be our main markets," Wing Tai chairman Cheng Wai Keung told reporters and analysts.
Wing Tai general manager Wong Siew Eng said in the next three to five years the company also expects its geographical cummulative profit share profile to change significantly.
Contribution from Singapore is expected to drop to 50 percent from the current 95 percent in favour of Hong Kong and Malaysia, Wong said.
She said Hong Kong's profit share is expected to soar to 30 percent from three percent and Malaysia to 20 percent from the present two percent.
Cheng said the company expects the hospitality sector to be an increasingly active contributor to group profit from 3-5 years onwards.

In the year ended June 30, 1996, Wing Tai's profit grew by 73 percent to Singapore $145 million (US$103 million). "This performance was mainly a result of profit recognition from successful property launches," Cheng said.
He pointed to two key developments during the year that helped the company shift to an "increasingly regional" profile.

The first was the award of the Kowloon Station Property Development Package One in Hong Kong. "The landmark project was timely, as it gave our presence in Hong Kong an excellent kick-start," Cheng said.

Wing Tai holds 30 percent of the commercial and residential project expected to be completed in the last quarter of 1999. Income from the project is expected from the financial year ending June 1999, Wong said.
The second development was in the service apartment area, Cheng said. "To date, we have secured projects in...Singapore, Malaysia and Jakarta, contibuting to aproximately 700 units."
Two of the four projects secured will be operational in 1997, Wong said.
Wing Tai expects to launch its first service apartment next year in Kuala Lumpur. Its service apartment in Singapore's Winsland House will also be completed next year.
Wong said Wing Tai's activities in its Suzhou, China residential, office and retail projects are currently at a relatively low level, "but long-term prospect are positive."
Wong said a planned issue of redeemable cumulative preference shares to raise S$150 million will help the company fund part of its future property investments and developments. (US$1=S$1.41)
